Cokanasiga Scores Twice as Bath Overcome Sale to Enter International Break in Fourth

Bath Ends Winless Run at the Recreation Ground

Joe Cokanasiga scored two tries to help Bath secure a victory over Sale, ending a three-match winless streak across all competitions. The hosts claimed a maximum of five points from the fixture, lifting them to fourth place in the standings as the domestic competition enters an international break.

Match Summary and Try Scorers

Bath established an early advantage through Henry Arundell, who marked his first Premiership appearance of the season by scoring within the opening three minutes after breaking through from the halfway line. Further tries from Tom de Glanville, Louis Hennessey, and Cokanasiga's double secured the bonus point for the hosts. Fly-half Finn Russell contributed four conversions and a penalty.

Despite trailing for much of the match, Sale managed to secure a losing bonus point thanks to late tries. Nathan Jibulu and Tom O'Flaherty crossed the line during the earlier phases, while Luke Cowan-Dickie and Elia Canakaivata added late scores in the final ten minutes. George Ford kicked four conversions for the visitors, who finished the match in eighth position following their third defeat of the campaign.

Reaction from the Camps

Bath director of rugby Johann van Graan told BBC Radio Bristol that his side successfully integrated multiple facets of their game, praising their defensive work and attacking phases.

Sale director of rugby Alex Sanderson noted that while his team displayed physical intent and created scoring opportunities, execution errors and defensive lapses in the wide channels proved costly before their late rally.
